Drilling to base level
The continuous auger screws into the soil. The soil plug remaining on the auger supports the wall of the bore – no separate support is needed.
Concreting through the drill stem
Withdrawn too fast! The concrete cannot fill the place of the auger – in the soft layer the pile narrows (necking).
The concrete is pumped under excess pressure through the inside of the stem; the concrete pushes the auger up with the soil plug while the rig pulls. The concrete pressure is measured continuously.
Reinforcement into the fresh concrete
Positioning, starting the casing
Installing the casing starts with rotation (or vibration).
Soil removal under the protection of the casing
The soil is removed with a drilling bucket; in granular soil the casing goes ahead of the excavation.
No water replacement: the external water pressure breaks the soil in at the base!
Below the groundwater the water removed is replaced in the bore.
Base cleaning
No loosened, settled soil may remain at the bottom of the bore – it would greatly reduce the base resistance.
Concreting, withdrawing the casing
The concrete is placed from the bottom up through a tremie pipe, while the casing is withdrawn step by step. The end of the pipe stays in the concrete throughout.
Large diameter, great depth: safe even in silty soil with a high water content – in return slower, with complex machinery.
The bore is filled with bentonite slurry – the slurry level is well above the groundwater table.
Soil removal with slurry support
The slurry level has dropped close to the groundwater table: the excess pressure is lost and the wall of the bore collapses.
The soil is removed with a drilling bucket. The slurry displaces the groundwater and supports the wall of the bore with its excess pressure.
Base cleaning, reinforcement
The concrete fills the bore from the bottom and displaces the lighter slurry upwards – the slurry is recovered.
Mainly for large-diameter, deep piles; in Hungary mostly for the foundations of long-span bridges.
Drilling with a short auger
The bore is not stable: because of the groundwater or the granular layer the wall collapses!
The short auger brings up the soil in cycles.
Concreting immediately
It must be concreted immediately after excavation – through a concreting hopper.
Simple and cheap – but only for a stable bore.
Lifting in the pile
The precast reinforced concrete pile is held vertical by the leader of the piling rig.
Refusal! ${M.P.blocks ? 'A tömbös feltöltésen' : 'A kemény agyagban'} the pile cannot get down to the design depth.
In the blocky fill
In the hard clay
The hammer blows drive the pile into the ground; the displaced soil is compacted – the base and shaft resistance increase.
Pile trimming
The protruding part is cut off – but the pile has not reached the design base level.
After driving, the pile head is broken back to the design level.
Fast and of high bearing capacity – but driving comes with significant noise and vibration.
Casing, concrete plug
A dry concrete plug approx. 1 m high is placed in the bottom of the 46–52 cm casing.
Driving with an internal drop hammer
The 3 t drop hammer rams the plug; through friction the plug drags the tube down to the bearing stratum.
Driving out the plug, bulb
The tube is fixed, the plug is driven out, and a widened base – the “bulb” – is rammed with further batches of concrete.
Concreting the shaft, withdrawing the casing
The casing is withdrawn while concrete is added and rammed. Because of the displacement, the finished pile is approx. 60 cm in diameter.
At the end of the hollow drill stem there is a special displacement drilling head.
Drilling by rotation and thrust
The head pushes aside and compacts the soil around itself – hardly any spoil comes to the surface.
displacement head
Concreting while withdrawing the stem
The concrete is placed under pressure through the drill stem, and the stem is withdrawn with rotation.
Reinforcement by vibration
No dynamic effect or noise; the displacement increases the specific bearing capacity.
Positioning with a small rig
The small rig can also work in places with difficult access and low headroom.
Drilling and grouting at once
A hollow steel bar with a sacrificial drill bit is drilled down (with extensions), with continuous cement grouting meanwhile.
The prefabricated reinforcement cage is vibrated down into the fresh concrete.
The reinforcement cage is lowered into the casing.
The reinforcement cage is lowered into the bore immediately.
The base is cleaned, then the reinforcement cage is lowered into the slurry.
The reinforcement cage is lowered into the casing; spacers ensure the concrete cover.
